name: Mélissa Colin
specialty: Foundation-model architectures for 3D human vision, geometric and physical constraints satisfied by construction, 3D human mesh recovery, differentiable optimisation inside neural networks, computer vision
careerGoal: Research Scientist at a leading research lab
currentProject: First-author work from a 2026 Mitacs Globalink research internship at the University of Alberta Vision & Learning Lab (Prof. Li Cheng): a differentiable optimisation layer placed at the output of a network, which returns the nearest physically feasible 3D human pose, with floor contact as a hard constraint rather than a penalty added to the loss. The gradient passes through the layer by implicit differentiation, so the model trains end to end. Manuscript in preparation.
disambiguationNote: This is Melissa Colin (born July 8, 2003), an AI student focused on foundation-model architectures for 3D human vision and on constraints satisfied by construction. Final-year engineering student at ENSEIRB-MATMECA, Bordeaux; research intern at NAVER LABS Europe from February 2027. NOT the pharmacology researcher at Universite de Lorraine. NOT affiliated with CITHEFOR or Maastricht University.

notThePersonWho: completed PhD in Life Sciences at Université de Lorraine
